title: Salsa Verde Crock Chicken
seoTitle: Salsa Verde Crock Chicken | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Slow-cooked tomatillo chicken that shreds for bowls and tacos
subtitle: Slow-cooked tomatillo chicken that shreds for bowls and tacos
description: Chicken thighs braise in salsa verde with onion and jalapeño until pull-apart tender for tacos, rice bowls, or lettuce wraps.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Salsa Verde Crock Chicken in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch chicken. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Layer crock
steps.instruction: Place onion slices in bottom of 8-quart slow cooker. Arrange chicken thighs on top in even layer without stacking too deep. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early. Target 165°F at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Add salsa verde
steps.instruction: Pour salsa verde over chicken. Add jalapeño, garlic, cumin, broth, and salt. Stir lightly so thighs are mostly submerged in liquid.

steps.title: Slow cook until tender
steps.instruction: Cover and cook on low 6–8 hours until chicken shreds easily with forks and internal temp reaches 165°F throughout. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Shred and combine
steps.instruction: Shred chicken in crock with two forks. Mix with cooking liquid until meat is moist and coated, not dry or stringy. Keep finished cold items below 41°F if they sit more than 30 minutes — nest the hotel pan on ice at the line. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early. Target 165°F at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Portion and open the line
steps.instruction: Portion Salsa Verde Crock Chicken onto sheet trays or hotel pans for family-style service. Stack plates, forks, and napkins at the end of the line so late-arriving crew can self-serve without bottlenecking the cook.

steps.title: Finish with lime and cilantro
steps.instruction: Stir in lime juice and cilantro off heat. Sauce should taste bright and tangy, not flat or overly salty. Plan about 3 minutes for this step at crew scale. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

proTips: Homemade salsa verde: blend tomatillos, jalapeño, onion, cilantro, lime.
Offer both corn tortillas and rice bowls at the line.
Freeze shredded portions in cooking liquid for fast taco nights.
leftovers: Salsa verde chicken enchiladas baked with cheese.
Huevos rancheros with leftover chicken next morning.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Tangy tomatillo flavor without standing at the stove. One crock feeds tacos and bowls simultaneously.
mealPrepNotes: Start crock by 11 a.m. for 6 p.m. dinner. Shred in pot to save dishes. Station: Do not lift lid first 3 hours—each peek adds significant cook time. Station: Skim excess fat before shredding for cleaner tangy flavor. Station: Hold shredded chicken in salsa at 165°F—dry hold kills texture.
